rationale: Compliance must be recorded at the time of surgery and infections followed for 30 days, which is a prospective observational design. A trial of the bundle is not possible because it is already standard care; the question is how reliably it is delivered and whether full delivery goes with fewer infections. The multicentre planning value (c1) shows that one year gives too few infections, so data collection runs for 24 months with a descriptive report at 12 months. Reporting follows STROBE.
alternatives: Retrospective extraction from operation notes (refused: normothermia and glucose are poorly recorded, and applicability cannot be judged later)
Cluster trial of bundle feedback (refused: one hospital)
Twelve-month study (refused: about 50 infections are too few for the adjusted association)
whyNotMoreComplex: Element-level causal claims would need far more events and would still be confounded by correlated elements; the design estimates full-bundle compliance and one adjusted association.

decision.statement: Pursue a 24-month prospective observational study of bundle compliance and 30-day surgical site infection in all colorectal resections, with compliance scored all-or-none over applicable elements (c3), day-30 post-discharge follow-up (c2), adjustment for emergency status and contamination (c4), and the multicentre association (c1) as the planning value.
decision.question: Should the working group measure bundle compliance prospectively and estimate its association with infection?

criteria.text: Full compliance has been associated with fewer infections, and compliance and infection can both be measured completely.
Recording compliance at the time of surgery cannot be done within two minutes.

gates.requirement: Quality council approval of prospective bundle data collection
gates.evidence: Approval QC-SSI-2026-4 dated 2026-08-18, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: REB determination for the study with publication permitted
gates.evidence: Exemption REB-EX-26-311 dated 2026-09-10, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Twelve-month descriptive audit of compliance without the infection association
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c4 from retrieved records; both gates are met on investigator-supplied records.

summary: Prospective observational study over 24 months recommended; both gates met.
